description: Baseline run of cpu_throughput bench (session setup commit). checks.sh bug (pipefail + grep no-match) made the gate fail spuriously; fixed in follow-up commit, tests actually pass.

asi.checks_fixed: checks.sh pipefail bug — grep with no matches returns 1 (fixed in c375769)
asi.phase_insight: bench variance across invocations ~7% (470k-504k). Need phase timings to know where the 22ms/batch goes.

description: Hydrate optimizations: (1) AHashSet for did/uri dedup, (2) resolve_profiles now returns HashMap<String, Arc<BlueskyProfile>> via a single get pass (was contains_key + per-message moka get), (3) hydrate_one became sync (removed its only await) with HashMap lookups instead of moka gets.

asi.hypothesis: hydrate-phase micro-opts: ahash dedup sets, single moka get pass returning profile map threaded into sync hydrate_one (removed per-message moka get + async future overhead)
asi.learnings: moka get vs contains_key — get may be slower (updates access time); resolve step showed no clear regression in clean runs. Machine load ~4.3 (Chrome/opencode) causes 5-10% run-to-run variance; bump measure.sh RUNS to 5.
asi.profile_note: Cost model per 10k batch: envelope parse 6.4ms floor, record serde_json Value tree +2ms, hydrate 4.5ms, serialize 5.6ms (msg 3.4 Value vs 2.9 OwnedValue, meta 1.8). simd-json has no RawValue support; OwnedValue refactor ceiling ~1.6ms total.

description: Switch CommitData.record from serde_json::Value to simd_json::OwnedValue. Parse now builds OwnedValue directly from simd-json's tape (record tree cost ~1ms less); serialization of the record via simd-json is faster. RecordView/accessors adapted (same API); fixtures+tests use simd_json::json!.

asi.hypothesis: Replace serde_json::Value record with simd_json::OwnedValue in CommitData.record — simd-json deserializes OwnedValue from its own tape ~1ms faster than building serde_json::Value, and serializes it faster.
asi.learnings: value-trait 0.10.1 has blanket impls (ValueObjectAccess for T) so .get() works on OwnedValue directly with simd_json::prelude in scope. serde_json::from_value still works for deserializing EnrichedRecord (OwnedValue: Deserialize).
asi.refactor_notes: Changed CommitData.record type, RecordView now a lens over &simd_json::OwnedValue (same accessor names via value_trait blanket impls + prelude), fixtures/tests json! → simd_json::json!. Record key ORDER in serialized output now hash order (halfbrown HashMap) vs sorted before — semantically irrelevant, byte counts unchanged.

description: Reuse simd-json scratch buffers across parse calls: parse_message now uses a thread-local simd_json::Buffers with to_tape_with_buffers + tape.deserialize instead of from_str (which re-allocates all scratch buffers per message). Parse dropped from ~8.4ms to ~5.2ms per 10k.

asi.hypothesis: simd-json allocates fresh scratch buffers (string_buffer, structural indexes, aligned input) per from_str call. Reuse a thread-local simd_json::Buffers across parse calls via to_tape_with_buffers + Tape::deserialize.
asi.implementation: thread_local PARSE_BUFFERS RefCell<Buffers> in jetstream.rs; parse_message now does text.to_string() + to_tape_with_buffers + tape.deserialize::<JetstreamMessage>(). Unsafe text.as_bytes_mut() is sound: simd-json rewrites escapes in place, result stays valid UTF-8. Note tape borrows the input so buffers borrow_mut scope is correct.
asi.learnings: Measured in isolation: buffered parse 5.2ms vs from_str 8.4ms per 10k messages (~38% of parse phase). The allocations were the dominant parse cost, not the tape walk.

description: Hydrate phase: switch profile/outcome maps from std HashMap (SipHash) to ahash::AHashMap, and merge the two RecordView extraction passes into one traversal (extract_refs_from_view).

asi.hypothesis: Profile/outcome maps were std::collections::HashMap (SipHash ~80ns/lookup); switch to ahash::AHashMap (~20ns). Also merged extract_mentioned_dids_from_view + extract_post_uris_from_view into one extract_refs_from_view traversal (record was traversed 3x via reply_refs/facets/embed).
asi.learnings: SipHash lookups in the hydrate per-message loop were measurable; AHashMap cut them. Note: merged traversal preserves dedup semantics (sort+dedup both Vecs, same as before).

description: hydrate_one: merge profiles.contains_key + get into a single get/match (one hash lookup instead of two per message).

asi.hypothesis: hydrate_one did contains_key + get (2 hash lookups per message); merge into a single get with match.
asi.learnings: Small but consistent win (~+0.6%). Serialize phase (~5.3ms) is now the wall — generic serde at ~1.3-1.8GB/s. Custom Serialize impls identical to derive output (no gain). Record raw-splice still blocked by serde's no-raw-JSON hook.

description: Clippy + fmt cleanup (CI uses -D warnings): #[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)] on PostFetchOutcome (matches existing Embed pattern), #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] on hot-path hydrate_one, cargo fmt --all.

asi.hypothesis: Perf-neutral cleanup: fix clippy warnings (CI uses -D warnings) — allow(large_enum_variant) on PostFetchOutcome, allow(too_many_arguments) on hydrate_one, cargo fmt. Measurement dip (674k vs 702k) is machine-load noise (runs 646-686k overlap previous session's 652-713k).
asi.learnings: CI: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check. Machine load varies ±5-8% between sessions.

description: Parse: combine thread-local Buffers + a reusable input Vec<u8> into one ParseScratch struct. Eliminates the per-message heap String allocation (saves ~0.2-0.3ms/10k) and removes the unsafe as_bytes_mut (Vec<u8> has no UTF-8 invariant).

asi.hypothesis: parse_message did text.to_string() (heap alloc per message) + unsafe as_bytes_mut. Replace with thread-local ParseScratch{ buffers, input: Vec<u8> } — one TLS lookup, reused input buffer (clear + extend_from_slice), removes the unsafe entirely.
asi.learnings: Nested thread_locals cost extra TLS lookups, so combine buffers+input into ONE thread-local struct. Borrow-checker needs destructuring (let ParseScratch{buffers,input} = &mut *scratch) for disjoint field borrows in to_tape_with_buffers. Vec<u8> avoids the String UTF-8 invariant question.

description: hydrate_one: hoist Span::current() to a single handle and record both did + cache_hit on it (was 2 TLS lookups per message). Perf-neutral; measurement polluted by machine load spike.

asi.hypothesis: hydrate_one called Span::current() twice per message (TLS lookup each); hoist one span handle and record both fields on it. Expected ~0.1-0.3ms.
asi.learnings: Machine load spiked during measurement (sysmond 66%, load ~4) — runs degraded 685k→602k mid-session. Direct binary runs before/after showed 663-692k, no regression. Span TLS cost smaller than estimated; change is neutral but keeps code cleaner.

description: Confirmation measurement on quieter machine: 695k msgs/sec steady (8-run median 674-712k). No code change since span-hoist commit; previous 636k was a load spike.

asi.hypothesis: Re-measurement of the span-hoist commit on a quieter machine — confirms ~695k steady-state (previous 636k log was a load-spike artifact).
asi.learnings: Steady-state performance ~695k msgs/sec = +47% over baseline. All phases at floor: parse 4.6ms, hydrate 3.1ms, serialize 5.3ms (bench-to_string allocation locked). 8-run direct median: 695k (674-712k).

description: Hydrate: remove redundant author_did String from MessageContext (was a clone of message.did). hydrate_one now borrows the did from the message for the profile lookup; saves one String allocation per message and simplifies the context struct.

asi.hypothesis: MessageContext stored author_did as a clone of message.did (redundant). Remove the field+param; hydrate_one borrows message.extract_did() for the profile lookup (which returns owned Arc clones), then moves message into the EnrichedRecord. Saves 1 String alloc per message.
asi.learnings: Borrow ends before the move thanks to NLL (last use is profiles.get(author_did) which returns owned clones). hydrate_one still 8 args incl self → keep the clippy allow.

description: Resolve profiles with borrowed keys: resolve_profiles now returns AHashMap<&str, Arc<BlueskyProfile>> keyed by references into the caller's dids Vec instead of cloning every did into owned String keys. Fewer allocations in the hydrate resolve path.

asi.hypothesis: resolve_profiles cloned every did into the returned map keys (10k String allocs). Return AHashMap<&str, Arc> with keys borrowing from the caller-owned dids Vec; hydrate lookups use did.as_str(). Saves 10k String allocs + shrinks map entries.
asi.learnings: Borrow-lifetime gotcha: fetched-profile keys must reference the input dids slice (index back via uncached_indexes), not the local uncached Vec (would be a return-referencing-local error). hydrator mention loop needed profiles.get(did.as_str()) for the &str-keyed map.

description: Confirmation measurement: 683-712k msgs/sec steady (+48-50% over baseline). No code change.

asi.hypothesis: Confirmation run; steady state 683-712k depending on machine load (10-run direct median 701k).
asi.learnings: Serialization phase is the hard wall: bench calls simd_json::to_string (per-call Vec alloc ~0.8ms, locked) + generic serde walk at ~1.35GB/s. serde_json measured slower. Custom Serialize impls are identical to derive output. No raw-JSON emit hook exists in serde/simd-json.

description: Quiet-machine confirmation: 8-run median 733k msgs/sec. Load-dependent band is 675-735k overall.

asi.hypothesis: Load dropped to ~2.4 → 8-run direct median 733k. measure.sh window caught a busier moment (675-706k). True steady-state ~690-735k, +45-55% over baseline.
asi.learnings: Machine load strongly modulates measurements (±15%). Direct 8-run medians are the most reliable; measure.sh 5-run median is close. Earlier noisy windows underestimated the real improvement.

description: Final steady-state measurement: median 722k msgs/sec (683-760k band), +52% over the 474k baseline. Serialize phase (5.2ms, bench to_string) is the remaining wall.

asi.final_state: 12-run: min 683k / median 722k / max 760k msgs/sec. Cumulative +52% over baseline (474k). All phases at practical floors: parse 4.8ms, hydrate 3.3ms, serialize 5.2ms.
asi.wrap_up: 14 experiments kept; CI-clean (clippy -D warnings 0, fmt, 209 tests); metric bench untouched; remaining ideas documented in .auto/ideas.md (raw-splice blocked by serde model, to_writer-shared-buffer is production-only win, parallel hydrate deliberately declined as benchmark-gaming).

description: Remove dead per-message Instant measurement in hydrate_one: hydration_time_ms always rounded to 0 in the batch design (fetching happens in resolve_profiles before hydrate_one), so the clock reads were pure overhead. Field stays default 0.

asi.hypothesis: hydrate_one measured per-message hydration_time_ms via Instant::now()+elapsed(). In the batch design all fetching happens in resolve_profiles/resolve_posts BEFORE hydrate_one, so the elapsed always rounds to 0 — the clock reads (~0.4-0.5ms/batch) measured nothing. Removed them; field stays default 0 (same output as before).
asi.learnings: 10-run median 728k (711-759k) vs prior 722k (683-757k) — min improved 683k→711k (less low-end variance). Small real win + code simplification.

description: Parse: use simd_json::serde::from_slice_with_buffers (single call) instead of to_tape_with_buffers + tape.deserialize (double Deserializer construction). Neutral per re-measurement, cleaner.

asi.hypothesis: parse_message used to_tape_with_buffers + Tape::deserialize (constructs the Deserializer, extracts the tape, then re-constructs a Deserializer from it). from_slice_with_buffers does it in one call (same internal work, less wrapper). Expected neutral-to-tiny-positive.
asi.learnings: A transient dip (665k) looked like a regression but a 12-run re-measure showed 723k median (676-761k) — same as before. Machine thermal/background spikes cause ±10% session swings; always re-run before concluding a regression.

description: Steady-state: 725.8k msgs/sec median (713-746k). Session docs updated; measure.sh now uses 7 runs for robustness.

asi.hypothesis: Steady-state confirmation with improved measure.sh (7 runs). 725.8k median, 713-746k band.
asi.learnings: Session steady state: ~725k msgs/sec (+53% vs 474k baseline). Everything at measured floors; remaining candidates all sub-1%. Next avenues if pursued: custom serde serializer tuned for these types (risky), or accept current state.
